findings.subject: phase-rep-07
findings.title: The declared source for demo-build.yaml (PLAN-021, doc-live-demo) does not name the roster or dispatch structure the scope line claims it does, and nothing in acceptance would catch the resulting inaccuracy.
findings.evidence: phase-rep-07 scope: "docs/08-governance/fleet/systems/demo-build.yaml - the PLAN-021 orchestrators and the creators and validators they dispatch, all lifecycle parent (R03)." PLAN-054 D3 repeats the same framing. The phase's only source for this file is doc-live-demo (PLAN-021). Reading PLAN-021 in full: it names three orchestrator agents generically (never by name) and says the build session (the coordinator, PROMPT-014) "dispatches the three orchestrator agents" -- it never enumerates which agents are creators/validators, and says 'eight demo agents' total. The real roster, in PROMPT-012 (`doc-prompt-demo-agent-roster-spec`, not a declared source), is ten: demo-orch-stage, demo-orch-data, demo-orch-content, demo-creator-py, demo-creator-web, demo-creator-docs, demo-validator-code, demo-validator-check, demo-adversary, demo-validator-web (`ls .claude/agents/ | grep demo-` confirms these ten files exist, plus two unrelated demo-agent-* files used elsewhere). Critically, PROMPT-018 (`doc-prompt-demo-build-delegation-pack`, also not sourced), line 34-37: "each phase's D0N-A (adversarial review, demo-adversary) and ... D02-W/D04-W/D05-W (Playwright browser checks, demo-validator-web) are dispatched by the coordinator ... not by the orchestrators." So two of the ten roles are dispatched by the coordinator directly, not by the orchestrators the scope line names as the dispatcher, and the coordinator itself -- the role PLAN-021 explicitly calls out as the one that "claims the phases ... dispatches the three orchestrator agents" -- is never named as a role anywhere in D3's table or phase-rep-07's scope.
findings.consequence: A developer building demo-build.yaml from the declared source alone will either omit the coordinator role (so no delegates-to/coordinates edge from coordinator to the three orchestrators can be modelled) or mis-attribute demo-adversary and demo-validator-web as dispatched by an orchestrator rather than the coordinator. Unlike the GOV-017 system, acceptance has no roster-fidelity test for demo-build.yaml (only "the three system files pass the schema and the integrity test", which checks internal reference resolution, not fidelity to PLAN-021/PROMPT-018), so an inaccurate model of this system would pass the phase's own acceptance undetected.
findings.minimal_fix: Add doc-prompt-demo-build-orchestration (PROMPT-014) and doc-prompt-demo-build-delegation-pack (PROMPT-018) to phase-rep-07's sources, and reword the scope line to name the coordinator as a role and state that demo-adversary and demo-validator-web are dispatched by the coordinator, not the orchestrators.

dispositions.reason: phase-rep-07's sources now include PROMPT-012 (doc-prompt-demo-agent-roster-spec), PROMPT-014 (doc-prompt-demo-build-orchestration) and PROMPT-018 (doc-prompt-demo-build-delegation-pack). Its scope names the coordinator, a top-level session running PROMPT-014, and PROMPT-012's ten agents. It also states that the coordinator itself dispatches demo-adversary and demo-validator-web (PROMPT-018, the completion gate) while the orchestrators dispatch the creators and the other two validators. A new acceptance line requires demo-build.yaml's roles to equal that roster and its coordinator edges to name the two gate agents. PLAN-054's phase table carries the same roster sentence.
